articles.title_orig: Heavy Rain and Wind Batter Northeast, Bringing Coastal Flooding
articles.title_zh: Heavy Rain and Wind Batter Northeast, Bringing Coastal Flooding
articles.content_orig:
An early-season nor'easter is hammering the East Coast this weekend with major coastal flooding, high surf, strong winds, rain and rip currents from North Carolina to New England, including Boston and the New York City tri-state area.
A full moon is happening this weekend as well, only making the coastal flooding situation worse.
For a complete tracker with all of the maps you need to stay updated on this storm, click here .
The nor'easter is lashing the mid-Atlantic and New England this weekend into early next week, and the flooding will continue to ebb and flow with the tides as the weekend progresses.
Coastal flooding is expected with major inundation, according to the National Weather Service from the Jersey shore to North Carolina's northern Outer Banks. Moderate inundation is expected across the coast of Massachusetts.
If you want to read about the events of the nor'easter on Saturday as they unfolded, click the link below.
Set The Weather Company as a 'Preferred Source' to get quicker access to the news you value.
( LIVE UPDATES RECAP: Nor'easter lashes the East Coast )
The map below shows current winds and rain.
Here's a general timeline of the storm and its impacts over the next several days. Boston is in the area of greatest concern for flooding and is now in a flood watch until 2 a.m. Tuesday. A detailed breakdown of the timing for the city and the entire region is below:
The map below shows coastal flood warnings that have been issued by the National Weather Service. These include Atlantic City, Long Island, the Norfolk metro area, Ocean City (Maryland and New Jersey), downtown Boston, Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket.
The most significant coastal flooding will include the Virginia Tidewater, as well as Chesapeake Bay and Delaware Bay. In these areas, water will be about 2-4 feet higher than normal at high tide.
As much as 3 feet of inundation will occur across Long Island's south and east bays.
(WATCH: Nor'easter waves slam stilt homes on the Outer Banks )
Given this repeated battering from high surf, beach erosion is expected along stretches of these beaches, potentially reaching extreme levels for some areas.
(MORE: Coastal flooding safety )
At least minor coastal high tide flooding will continue for parts of New England, lasting through Sunday.
One bit of good fortune with this storm is that its rainfall is being spread out over several days, rather than arriving in one short deluge.
That means any flood risk should be localized to traditional urban trouble spots.
That rainfall could also add to any coastal flooding at high tide through Sunday.
HIgh wind warnings are in effect for parts of the Jersey Shore, Long Island and eastern Connecticut. In these areas, gusts up to 60 mph are possible on Sunday.
In these areas, tree damage and power outages are most likely. Ground soaked from the nor'easter's rain, as well as trees that still have leaves, will only enhance this threat of tree damage and outages.
Otherwise, occasional gusts from 40 to 50 mph are possible from Virginia to other parts of coastal New England. Some sporadic power outages and tree limb damage are also possible in these areas.

( MORE: Nor'easter impacts on Major League Baseball's weekend )
Some gusts topped 40 mph along the coast from southern Massachusetts down to the Virginia Tidewater Wednesday as the storm system started to develop in its early stages.
And those persistent winds piled up water from the ocean and bays along parts of the coast.
Minor to moderate coastal flooding was reported from parts of the Jersey Shore to southeast Virginia during Wednesday's morning and evening high tides.
Flooding was reported Wednesday morning in downtown Norfolk, Smithfield and Suffolk, Virginia, according to the National Weather Service.
Widespread gusts of 30-45 mph were ongoing as of Thursday evening, with peak gusts over 45 mph reported along the coast of North Carolina.
Those persistent winds were piling up water from the ocean and bays along parts of the coast. Water levels reached major flood stage during high tide Thursday evening.
A 16-mile stretch of North Carolina Highway 12 on the Outer Banks is closed in both directions due to ocean overwash. Specifically, the road is closed from Sea Oats Drive to Oregon Inlet Road in Dare County.
Rising waters forced the cancellation of the Oceans Calling Festival in Maryland.
Notably, a peak wind gust of 74 mph was recorded in Surf City, New Jersey. Another notable wind gust of 81 mph was reported at Montauk Point, New York. Wind gusts over 50 mph have been clocked across the Northeast Saturday, including from southern Cape Cod to parts of Long Island, coastal and southern New Jersey, the Delaware coast and the Delmarva Peninsula, and a few weather stations even recorded gusts over 60 mph, including one at Nantucket Memorial Airport.
New York City's JFK Airport reported a gust of 56 mph. These winds have pushed water into numerous roads in the New York metro area and caused major travel delays. Saturday afternoon brought 25 river gauges to major flood stage during high tide.
The highest water levels happened with Saturday's high tides, boosted by Saturday's full moon. The moon has a direct impact on the tides, and when we are in a full moon, it makes the high tides even higher.
With some of the highest astronomical tides of the month ongoing, this nor'easter's coastal flooding is only exacerbated.
Rainfall of 1-3 inches of rain has been reported so far.
You might think it is too early for a nor’easter, but the criteria for a nor’easter are met more often than you would think.
A nor’easter simply means that the winds blow into an area from the northeast. For the Northeast, that usually means an area of low pressure is just off the coast, which brings the winds in this direction.
(More: What is a nor’easter? )
Most people usually think of snow and ice with nor’easters and that is because nor’easters do tend to occur more in the late fall and winter.
The most notable nor’easters tend to bring heavy snow because these lows move up along the Gulf Stream, tapping into the warm ocean. This warm, moist air then clashes with the cold air over the Northeast to create heavy snowfall. Fortunately, this one is occurring way earlier, so it is all rain this time.

articles.title_orig: Men arrested in major incident at UK air base used by US
articles.title_zh: Men arrested in major incident at UK air base used by US
articles.content_orig:
Several men have been arrested on suspicion of crimes related to explosives at a village near an air base used by U.S. forces, police in southwestern England said on Sunday.
Police in Gloucestershire said it had declared a major incident and evacuated "a number of properties" in the Whelford area following the arrest of "several men on suspicion of offences under the explosives act," referring to the country's laws around explosives.
The authorities also said a bomb disposal team were on site examining a number of vehicles.
Some local residents were evacuated, police said, and a cordon was established but the incident is said to be "contained."
The town of Whelford is close to RAF Fairford, a base that American forces have used for strictly limited strikes during the war with Iran. After the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran on Feb. 28, the U.K. government allowed the American military to use the Fairford base to strike Iranian missile sites.
However, police did not confirm to the Associated Press whether the arrests were linked to the base.
A spokesperson for the U.S. Air Force said its personnel based at RAF Fairford "remain vigilant" but would not discuss specific force protection measures for security reasons.
"We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families," the spokesperson said.
Security measures have been significantly increased in recent days at the air baise, according to an eyewitness quoted by the Reuters news agency who said there had been more roadblocks and armed police preventing access.
A spokesperson for the U.K. government thanked emergency services for acting quickly and added that it would be "inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing."
This is a breaking news story. Check back for updates.

articles.title_orig: Anger grows across Spain after elderly woman evicted from her home of 70 years
articles.title_zh: Anger grows across Spain after elderly woman evicted from her home of 70 years
articles.content_orig:
An 87-year-old Spanish woman was forcibly evicted Wednesday from the Madrid apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years, in a case that highlights a growing housing crisis in the country.
Video showed Maricarmen Abascal, who is a wheelchair user, being taken out of the building in the Spanish capital’s Retiro neighborhood on a stretcher and driven away in an ambulance.
Supporters had gathered outside her building overnight on Friday, with dozens of police officers holding them back as some tried to stop the eviction from going ahead. In a social media video posted Friday by the Madrid tenants union, Abascal gave thanks for the support she had received.
Abascal’s lawyer, Beatriz Duro, described the force used in the eviction as “completely disproportionate and unnecessary” and decried the intransigence of the building’s owners.
The case has brought new attention to an ongoing housing crisis in major cities across Spain, as gentrification has caused rents to skyrocket and the stock of affordable housing to shrink, leading to fierce public anger.
On Saturday, tens of thousands of people marched through the streets of Madrid to protest the eviction, some setting off flares. They carried placards reading “Not one more eviction, not one less neighbor, we are all Maricarmen” and “right to housing at a fair price.”
At the end of the march, protesters sat down in the Puerta del Sol plaza, some pitching tents. They remained in place early Sunday as dozens of activists staged a sit-in. A model of a vulture, decrying so-called “vulture funds,” hung above the camp.
Earlier in the week, tenants unions and other housing groups held protests and rallies in 16 cities, including Granada, Logroño and Zaragoza.
An investment fund acquired Abascal’s building in 2018 and sought a steep increase in her rent, and she had been fighting eviction for more than five years, according to the Madrid tenants union.
Duro said court officials and representatives of the fund, Urbagestión, had refused to suspend the eviction despite a pending court filing, humanitarian appeals and evidence that public authorities were working to secure alternative accommodation.
“They’re all inhumane,” Abascal said in a Spanish television interview the day before her eviction. “It’s as if I’m living with a machete at the back of my neck, ready to be chopped off at any moment.”
Duro also said an anonymous individual had offered to cover the rent payments, but the landlord declined to sign a new lease.
“We’ve been trying to negotiate with the landlords right up until the last moment, and they’ve flatly refused everything,” she said, decrying “a lack of humanity” in her treatment and “all these public resources” channeled into enabling the eviction.
Urbagestión did not respond to a request for comment.
The fresh wave of anger comes after protests in recent years against overtourism in Barcelona, where activists say a surge in apartments being used for short-term vacation rentals has contributed to a shortage of affordable housing.
The European Union announced new rules earlier this month aimed at tackling the housing crunch caused by short-term rentals in tourism hot spots.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described the eviction as “a social tragedy that we cannot accept either as a country or, of course, from the perspective of public institutions.”
Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Wednesday, Sánchez accused Madrid’s conservative regional government of pursuing luxury penthouses while ignoring demand for social housing.
Irene Hernández López, a 31-year-old test engineer living and renting in Chamberí, about 2 miles from Retiro, said what had happened to Abascal was “outrageous,” and she is worried similar evictions were already happening to other tenants around the city.
“Housing has become a product that people do business with,” she told NBC News. “It no longer matters that it’s your personal world, where you live and where you do your life.”
Hernández López, who pays 500 euros ($570) for a room in an apartment she shares with two others, said she was currently looking to move because the property was old and needs repairs, but that the rental market in Madrid was “terrible,” with prices “rising extremely quickly” and very little available.
“Some rooms are 500 euros or 600 euros and you think, ‘How am I supposed to live here? How can I pay 500 euros for this?’” she said. “I do think prices should be regulated, because wages aren’t going up while housing prices keep increasing. I don’t know how we’re supposed to keep going.”
Dan Nicander, secretary-general for the International Union of Tenants, said the situation in Spain was something his organization had seen in many countries in Europe.
“It’s a part of the financialization problem, seeing housing as an asset more than a home to people,” he told NBC News.
It’s “really tough” for the people living in the houses to do anything about it, he added, saying the responsibility lay with  politicians “to regulate the market in a way that it shouldn’t be that easy to buy and invest and then not [be] using the houses as homes.”
“Housing is a right,” he said. “It’s a fundamental right, first and foremost. It shouldn’t be a commodity.”
Jamie Gray is a senior desk editor for NBC News based in London.
Freddie Clayton is a freelance journalist based in London.

articles.title_orig: At least 27 people killed in two shootings in South African townships
articles.title_zh: At least 27 people killed in two shootings in South African townships
articles.content_orig:
At least 27 people have been killed and more than 20 wounded in two shootings in two South African townships, according to police.
In the first incident late on Saturday, at least 17 people were killed and 15 wounded in a shooting at a tavern in Wedela southwest of Johannesburg.
Police said they were searching for eight suspects, who were “reportedly armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols”. The motive for the shooting remained unknown, and no arrests were announced.
Early on Sunday, gunmen killed at least 10 people and wounded 11 at a store in Lwandle near Cape Town.
The shootings took place just days after a shooting at a house party near the city of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.
In the first incident, police said the attack began about 9:30pm (19:30 GMT) on Saturday in Extension 3, Wedela, in Gauteng province’s West Rand district.
The gunmen fired at people gathered outside the tavern before going inside, where more shots were fired. Investigators said some customers were searched during the attack and had their mobile phones taken.
The suspects then escaped in two vehicles. Two other vehicles were burned during the incident.
Captain Tintswalo Sibeko said detectives and specialist police units had been assigned to identify and find the eight suspects, with police opening 17 murder cases and 15 attempted murder cases as well as two cases related to property damage.
In the second incident, police said they were searching for multiple suspects after the shooting that took place after midnight on Sunday.
South Africa records persistently high levels of violent crime, including killings involving firearms.
The government has faced sustained pressure to improve public safety, particularly in major urban areas where police have carried out additional operations against gun crimes.

articles.title_orig: Jalen Brunson makes Knicks history hosting ‘SNL’ season 52 premiere
articles.title_zh: Jalen Brunson makes Knicks history hosting ‘SNL’ season 52 premiere
articles.content_orig:
NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, of the 2026 championship-winning New York Knicks, kicked off the 52nd season of “Saturday Night Live.”
During Saturday’s hoops-heavy show, Brunson delivered a monologue in which he promised to approach his “SNL” performance with the same strategy he used during Knicks’ NBA Finals games.
“The first three quarters of the show are going to be god-awful,” he said. “The last sketch is going to be amazing.”
The monologue featured “SNL” veteran Kenan Thompson as ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith, invited by Brunson so the player could “get some closure” after Smith had expressed doubts about his abilities.
Jalen Brunson brings Knicks players to 'SNL'
“I am man enough to admit that I was wrong when the New York Knickerbockers signed you and I did not think that you were the answer,” Thompson’s Smith said. “Nor did I believe that you could deliver the team’s first championship since 1973, when I was only 5 years old.”
Knicks teammates Josh Hart, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Karl-Anthony Towns made cameos to portray members of the studio audience chosen to ask questions of the point guard.
“Can you foul out of ‘SNL?’” Towns asked.
In the recorded sketch “High School Musical the New Generation,” Brunson portrayed a new student who wanted to join the school’s basketball team. He was welcomed with a musical number on the court that culminated with a team member portrayed by “SNL” featured player Jeremy Culhane singing that he was about to “take the shot.”
It was at that point that his attempt at scoring was rejected by Brunson, with the ball slamming against his forehead. Each subsequent attempt at a basket by Culhane’s character was met with over-the-top rejection. Soon, Brunson was defeating the team by weaving through defender traffic and scoring easily.
The NBA player concluded by swooping in to steal Culhane’s love interest (played by featured player Veronika Slowikowska) during another musical number, showing that even his singing chops were better than the ones of Culhane’s character. “Yeah, I think I’m going to hook up with this guy,” Slowikowska’s character said of the new student.
Brunson is the fifth NBA star to host the storied sketch comedy show, joining coach Bill Russell and legendary players Michael Jordan, Charles Barkley and LeBron James in sharing that status.
He averaged 32.6 points per game in the NBA Finals to help his team win its first championship in 53 years.
Saturday’s show also marked the first “SNL” season for two new featured players , Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter, after it bid farewell to cast member Chloe Fineman and writer Martin Herlihy, who also appeared in a number of sketches.
Fineman landed a role on “Myron Bolitar,” a Netflix drama series based on Harlan Coben’s thriller novels about a former basketball star who reinvents himself as a sports agent. Netflix announced the show started filming in New York City in July.
The musical guest Saturday was Katseye, the K-pop-influenced act composed of six women from around the world but often performing as a quintet and quartet due to hiatuses. The act was put together under a partnership between Geffen Records and South Korea’s HYBE Entertainment, home of BTS.
Katseye performed a pair of songs, “Animal” and “Hootie Frutti,” and appeared as judges in a recorded sketch that spoofed season two of the talent competition TV show “The Debut: Dream Academy.”
“SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.
Dennis Romero is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.

articles.title_orig: College football winners, losers in Week 4: Iowa emerges as Big Ten title threat, John Mateer struggles again
articles.title_zh: College football winners, losers in Week 4: Iowa emerges as Big Ten title threat, John Mateer struggles again
articles.content_orig:
Week 4 marks the formal start of conference play across college football , and the big-time matchups delivered. No. 17 Iowa pulled a stunner against No. 18 Michigan to win at Michigan Stadium for the first time since 2010 on the last play.
But while there's been plenty of highs, a few high-profile players struggled in big moments. Trinidad Chambliss was unable to keep up the magic against Florida , while Oklahoma's John Mateer collapsed against Georgia . The ACC race also took a wild turn after Wake Forest upset Louisville .
In the night slate, a few more titans fell as No. 12 USC, No. 13 Penn State and No. 23 Texas A&M all dropped. The losses shake up conference title and postseason pictures, but can teams recover? Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 4.
Expectations were low for the Aggies when they traveled to face No. 10 LSU. But in one fell swoop, a 35-6 loss, No. 23 Texas A&M's season effectively ended. Quarterback Marcel Reed was regrettably the primary culprit, completing a paltry 10 of 26 passes for 106 yards and an interception. The backup, Brady Hart, threw an interception on his only pass attempt.
As if that wasn't bad enough, Texas A&M allowed more than 300 yards passing and nearly 200 yards rushing. Frankly, the Aggies are just a bad football team at this point. Outside of a few talented wide receivers, who can't get the ball due to bad quarterback play, it's hard to find a single advantage Texas A&M can create against opponents.
No. 1 Texas, No. 8 Alabama and No. 14 Tennessee are still on the schedule, along with a road trip to Oklahoma. Will the Aggies make a bowl game?
The Cowboys officially turned the page on their season-opening loss to Tulsa by storming back from an early deficit to beat West Virginia 41-24 on the road. The Mountaineers were right on the edge of the rankings last week after beating No. 25 Virginia, and took a 14-3 lead early in the second quarter.
But when faced with adversity, quarterback Drew Mestemaker and wide receiver Wyatt Young again rose to the occasion. Young was unstoppable with eight catches for 192 yards and a touchdown in the win. Mestemaker shook off an interception to finish with 389 yards on only 27 pass attempts, 270 yards of which came in the second half.
The win over West Virginia was Oklahoma State's first Big 12 win in more than 1,000 days, snapping an 18-game losing streak. The last win was amazingly before the Cowboys played in the 2023 Big 12 title game. A new era is afoot.
Once again, USC was presented with the opportunity to get over the hump. After knocking Dante Moore out of the game with a dirty play, they were even playing at home against a backup quarterback. But when the game was decided, the Trojans were again too soft.
USC faced multiple opportunities to extend drives, but went 2 of 11 on third down. The Trojans failed to contain backup Dylan Raiola on fourth down and got bullied in high-leverage spots. This Trojans team is young, but excuses just keep piling up every year. With No. 5 Indiana, No. 7 Ohio State and No. 13 Penn State left on the schedule, when will it happen?
The Badgers needed something positive to happen in the Luke Fickell era. Old Dominion quarterback transfer Colton Joseph was ready to deliver. In the last 3:31, Joseph threw two touchdown passes to stun No. 13 Penn State, including a 72-yard pass to Jacob Harris with only 73 seconds remaining. It was the most complete defensive performance we've seen the Badgers put together, holding Penn State to only 233 yards. This was the kind of game Fickell was hired to win. There's a long season ahead, but can Fickell build on it?
Iowa's win against No. 18 Michigan to stay undefeated was a perfect Kirk Ferentz football game. The Hawkeyes puttered about for the first 40 minutes of play, only staying within striking distance because of a 99-yard kickoff return for a touchdown. And then, Hank Brown came to life.
The Hawkeyes got one of the great plays in program history, a game-winning touchdown with no time left on the clock by Brown to Reece Vander Zee for an unbelievable touchdown. The win was the first for Iowa in Michigan Stadium since 2010. More importantly, it seriously launched the No. 17 Hawkeyes into the Big Ten title and postseason conversation. With conference frontrunners Ohio State and Oregon already possessing losses, Iowa could easily crash the party.
Playing Georgia is never a recipe for success, but Oklahoma's QB1 put together one of the most stunningly poor performances of the season. After going down 14-0 in the second quarter, Mateer dropped one of the worst fumbles you'll ever see that turned third-and-goal into a Georgia defensive touchdown. He threw another interception, and then dropped the ball yet again to set up a short 11-yard touchdown drive for Georgia.
By the time the dust settled, Oklahoma was trailing 28-0 at halftime, part of a 41-13 loss against the Bulldogs in Athens. Statistically, Mateer was able to fight back in garbage time to finish with a respectable stat line, but the damage was done.
Oklahoma coach Brent Venables acknowledged that he considered making a change at halftime , but backup Whitt Newbauer has never played real snaps. There's no real answer on this Sooners roster, and Mateer is the face of the dysfunction.
CHRIS COLE HOUSE CALL 🏠 📺: ESPN pic.twitter.com/wNOacZCjqI
The Gators announced their return to major college football under Jon Sumrall on Saturday, finishing off an emphatic 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss . The Gators obliterated the Rebels behind a combined 268 yards and four touchdowns rushing from Jadan Baugh and Duke Clark , finishing with more than 300 yards on the ground as a team.
While an emotional letdown was expected for the Rebels after the dramatic win over Lane Kiffin and LSU last weekend, Florida looks the part of a serious national contender for the first time in years. The Gators still have No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Georgia on the schedule, but the Florida team we saw in Week 4 can hang with anyone.
The Cardinals can't make anything easy. One week after taking control of the ACC championship race with a win over SMU, Louisville lost a stunner against a streaking Wake Forest squad 30-27. With the loss, the Cardinals are no longer an at-large contender for the College Football Playoff field with two early losses. SMU still has a shot, and there are a few loose undefeated ACC teams left, but Louisville looked like the top competition to Miami . Now, things are much more complicated.
Boise State officially took their place as kings of the Group of Six race after obliterating Western Michigan 32-7 in a marquee matchup. articles.title_orig: No. 21 Florida serves notice to the rest of the SEC with its takedown of No. 4 Ole Miss
articles.title_zh: No. 21 Florida serves notice to the rest of the SEC with its takedown of No. 4 Ole Miss
articles.content_orig:
Last December, Florida athletic director Scott Stricklin did more than just kick the proverbial Lane Kiffin tires.
But when it was clear that he'd be headed to Baton Rouge, Stricklin turned to, at that point, a little-known former Kentucky linebacker who'd led Troy and Tulane to successful seasons. Nine months later, Jon Sumrall's Gators are the toast of college football after a drubbing of the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday . Florida's ability to control the line of scrimmage and move the ball on the ground may present serious problems for the rest of the league.
Despite a 24-point win over a top-five team Saturday, Sumrall quipped to reporters afterward, "We have not arrived."
No, Jon, you have. Florida vaults into our Top 10 at No. 3.
Plenty other wildness transpired on the fourth full Saturday of college football. In the Big Ten, for instance, Iowa (over Michigan) and Wisconsin (over Penn State) picked up comeback wins on the road, and Oregon gashed through USC's defense even without starting quarterback Dante Moore . In the SEC, the Longhorns remain our top-ranked squad after beating Tennessee, Alabama QB Keelon Russell seems like the real deal and OU's Brent Venables owes the Sooners back that contract extension. If you're wondering why more than half of our Top 10 is from the SEC, look at the non-conference power league records (the SEC was the only power conference with a winning record — 10-2 — against the others over the first three weeks).
Florida quarterback Aaron Philo had plenty reason to celebrate after the Gators' blowout win over Ole Miss on Saturday. (Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images)
In the Big 12, Utah cracked our Top 10. In fact, are the Utes the best of the Big 12? They've certainly played the toughest schedule yet of the challengers in the conference. With a win at Louisville, Wake Forest made it more difficult to answer a vexing question: Who the heck will challenge Miami in the ACC?
Let's hit the rankings, which, no, don't yet include Indiana (wins over North Texas, Howard, Western Kentucky and Northwestern don't get you ranked).
This week: beat Tennessee 20-17
No program in the country has the combination of two wins like Texas: Ohio State and at Tennessee. The Longhorns tried to cough it up late in Neyland Stadium, but they hung on to give QB Arch Manning a win at a special place (he wears jersey No. 16 because of uncle Peyton 's years in Knoxville). In an odd stat, Arch was sacked more times (6) than he threw incompletions (five). His 18-yard, third-down strike to Ryan Wingo on Texas' eight-play, 60-yard touchdown drive helped Steve Sarkisian's guys take a 10-point lead.
This week: beat Illinois 42-19
Last week, the Heisman Trophy seemed destined to head to Oxford and into the hands of QB Trinidad Chambliss. This week, it feels like it's right back to where it was originally: in Columbus in the glue-coated hands of Jeremiah Smith. The Buckeyes receiver and future NFL top-10 pick continued a heater of a season with 217 yards, 12 catches and four touchdowns on Saturday. He's up to more than 600 yards through four games and seven scores. He's a magician with his hands, catching nearly everything within a 2-mile radius.
This week: beat Ole Miss 52-28
Shocked? Don't be. The Gators have two wins in very impressive ways, scoring 44 points in a win at Auburn and then 52 against Ole Miss in The Swamp. First-year coach Jon Sumrall's team plays a physical brand of football that's fun to watch. They've rushed for nearly 550 yards in consecutive SEC games. That's no easy task. QB Aaron Philo is playing smart, consistent football and the Gators look like legit contenders in the league.
This week: beat Central Michigan 52-3
QB Darian Mensah's numbers through his first four games are simply absurd. Get this: He's got 12 incompletions — twelve! — and 14 touchdowns. Don't ignore that he's thrown for at least 330 yards twice, too. His favorite target, Malachi Toney (Baby Jesus!) caught another six passes for 120 yards on Saturday. The Hurricanes are as explosive as they've been the last few years. Can they continue the onslaught against a Clemson team that's, sort of, found some momentum?
Alabama QB Keelon Russell put on a show Saturday with four passing touchdowns and a rushing touchdown in a blowout win over South Carolina. (David Leong-Imagn Images)
This week: beat South Carolina 49-18
Next week: at Mississippi State
Perhaps it's time to start talking about QB Keelon Russell in relation to the Heisman Trophy, no? He's completing more than 70 percent of his passes, has eight touchdowns and two picks. On Saturday against the Gamecocks, Russell misfired on just six passes and threw four touchdowns. He's got plenty of pieces around him too. Kane Wommack's defense held South Carolina to a 21 percent clip on third downs.
This week: lost to Florida 52-28
The Rebels need the bye next week. After an emotional victory against former coach Lane Kiffin and LSU, they laid the egg in Gainesville without star running back Kewan Lacy. The Gators' defense swallowed Ole Miss' ground attack and pressured Trinidad Chambliss just enough. But the most concerning thing for Pete Golding is his defense, which was exploited earlier this year against Louisville, nearly collapsed in the second half against LSU and allowed almost 500 yards on Saturday.
This week: beat Purdue 49-10
Next week: at North Carolina
The Irish's schedule isn't glamorous so far. In fact, they haven't beaten a team that will finish ranked inside the top 25 at the end of the season (at least that's our assumption about Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State and Purdue). But the wins are fairly dominant and despite the struggles at times to run the football, Marcus Freeman's defense is one salty group. They entered third in the country in total D — a ranking that won't move much after Purdue's 218 yards.
This week: beat Oklahoma 41-13
The Bulldogs haven't played the toughest schedule so far, which is why they're at No. 8. But between QB Gunner Stockton and Kirby Smart's defense, they appear to be legitimate SEC title contenders — again. On Saturday, they forced the Sooners into a plethora of mistakes, including two fumbles, an interception and a turnover on downs. It's no fun playing against the Dawgs defense, despite NIL and the portal making it more difficult for them to stockpile front-seven depth.
This week: beat Missouri 31-24
Get ready to hear a whole lot about a Mississippi kid named Kamario Taylor, the Bulldogs' electric sophomore starting quarterback. He's slung 14 touchdowns and just two picks and, most recently on Saturday, put up 360 yards passing against Missouri in State's first top-25 win in more than a decade. Are the Bulldogs perfect? No. The defense can be exploited but former head coach Zach Arnett, the defensive coordinator, has the unit playing good enough.
This week: beat Iowa State 31-17
Welcome to the Top 10, Utes! They nearly let a 17-point lead slip away, but QB Devon Dampier showed just how slippery he can be. Most folks thought Dampier might follow Kyle Whittingham to Ann Arbor. Not so fast! He stuck around with new coach Morgan Scalley, who's got Utah playing its always-dependable D. On Saturday, RB Wayshawn Parker had a breakout performance (18 carries for 174 yards and three total TDs).

articles.title_orig: Trump rejects Iran’s seven-day roadmap to end war and reopen Hormuz
articles.title_zh: Trump rejects Iran’s seven-day roadmap to end war and reopen Hormuz
articles.content_orig:
Araghchi ignores Trump, waits for mediators’ response on Hormuz
United States President Donald Trump has rejected a plan submitted by Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, as Tehran continued to insist that only diplomacy can solve the conflict between the two countries.
Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said on Saturday that Iran wants to make a deal to open the vital maritime corridor immediately only “because they are losing so badly”.
“They want to make a deal, and I think that’s fine. I’d like to make a deal, too,” he said. But the proposal put forth by Iran “would not be acceptable,” he said.
The plan by Iran, announced on Friday at the United Nations General Assembly, calls for the US to release frozen Iranian funds, lift oil sanctions and end its naval blockade on Iranian ports.
Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s foreign minister, said at the time that those steps could be completed within four or five days, clearing the way for the strait to reopen and for negotiations on a final agreement to begin by the seventh day.
Araghchi responded to Trump’s rejection in a post on his Telegram channel on Saturday, saying Iran “will not back down” on its conditions.
“We have seen the first reaction from the US president, but nothing has been conveyed to us from the mediators yet,” Araghchi wrote, adding that Trump had a history of making “contradictory” statements.
He said Iran was “waiting for the definitive opinions to be conveyed to us by the mediators” and would “make a decision based on that”. He added that “only a negotiated solution” can get the US “out of this deadlock”.
US officials had signalled on Friday that Trump would reject the proposal. The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed US officials, reported that Trump was “privately sceptical” that Tehran would meet his demands. He reportedly told aides that he expects a renewed bombing campaign on Iran after the US midterm elections in November.
Al Jazeera’s Mike Hanna, reporting from Washington, DC, said the Iranian proposal appears “dead in the water”. But he noted Trump has offered no alternative.
“The one thing that has been made clear by President Trump is that he is content to stay in the status of limbo,” Hanna said, “despite concerns from much of the American public that the Iran conflict is turning into another ‘never-ending war’.”
Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway critical to global oil supplies, shortly after the US and Israel launched their war on February 28. Iranian attacks on vessels in the waterway have since sharply curtailed shipping.
The US has responded with an economic blockade on Iran and threats of secondary sanctions against airports and companies doing business with Iranian airlines – measures that have already prompted the United Arab Emirates, Iraq and Oman to cancel flights .
Earlier in the week, Araghchi met with Steve Witkoff, Trump’s envoy, to lay out conditions for ending the war, which would also include waiving oil sanctions and establishing a regional ceasefire covering Lebanon and Yemen.
Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian, who was also in New York for the UNGA, said on Saturday that Tehran no longer trusted negotiations with Washington, citing past rounds of talks that were followed by military strikes and new sanctions.
“We have no trust in the American side and do not know on what basis an understanding can be reached with it,” Pezeshkian told Al Jazeera.
He denied that Iran bore responsibility for the closure of the strait, saying the US had “closed the routes before us”. He said the waterway would reopen to commercial shipping if negotiations succeeded in ending the war.
Ross Harrison, a senior fellow at the Middle East Institute, said Iran’s proposal was intended chiefly as a gesture of goodwill.
“I think they are trying to show the willingness to talk and negotiate,” he told Al Jazeera. “That’s what’s important for their home audience back in Iran, and it’s also important for the American public.”
Harrison said Iran’s leaders likely anticipated Trump’s rejection, since the proposal closely mirrored the now failed memorandum of understanding signed in June that Tehran believes Washington had undermined.
“I don’t think they were surprised at all” by Trump’s move, he said.

articles.title_orig: ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts
articles.title_zh: ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts
articles.content_orig:
After eight years and countless entries in the expanding onscreen universe, Star Wars is revisiting the Skywalker family with its next project.
Deadline can confirm that Lucasfilm has tapped Skeleton Crew co-creator Jon Watts (director of Spider-Man: Homecoming , Spider-Man: Far From Home and Spider-Man: No Way Home ) to helm the first installment in a new trilogy of the Skywalker Saga, which is being penned by Simon Kinberg ( X-Men: Dark Phoenix , Prime’s Mr. & Mrs. Smith ).
Kinberg, who previously co-created the DisneyXD animated series Star Wars Rebels (2014-’18), has been working on the new trilogy since 2018, with Daisy Ridley reportedly eyed to reprise her role as Rey, as it will serve in the next chapter of the Skywalker Saga.
The project reportedly has not yet received a greenlight from parent company Disney.
Beginning with Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope in 1977 and the sequels Episode V — The Empire Strikes Back (1980) and Episode VI — Return of the Jedi (1983), the Skywalker Saga continued with the prequel trilogy Episode I — The Phantom Menace (1999), Episode II: Attack of the Clones (2002) and Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (2005).
Most recently, the franchise left off the Skywalker Saga with the latest trilogy, Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens (2015), Episode VIII — The Last Jedi (2017) and Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker (2019), which was led by Ridley’s Rey.
Since the last chapter in the Skywalker Saga, the Star Wars franchise has expanded with films and streaming series set throughout the onscreen universe, with the next installment Star Wars: Starfighter set for a May 28, 2027 premiere.
Lucasfilm had no comment. Knight Edge Media was first to report the news.
Get our Breaking News Alerts and Keep your inbox happy.
Star Wars was never a franchise. It was a serialized story told over six films, based on the interests and inspirations of one very peculiar individual. Whatever you think of his craft, Lucas was focused on delivering a grand mythology, which foregrounded a family tragedy against an epic background of fantasy, adventure and political allegory. No one other than him has delivered anything remotely like it in the history of the medium.
Expecting that anyone else could do the same was Disney’s big mistake. In fact, like many observers and even some fans, they fundamentally misunderstood what made the saga so successful. Handing it over to people who also didn’t get it like Abrams – who basically approached the job as a fanboy – ended in retread, deconstruction and chaos.
You can expand on ideas in the story, like Gilroy did to great effect, or you can tell adventure stories backward or forward in time, but none of it is going to get you the same unexpected epic that only Lucas was uniquely placed to tell. So, yeah, I expect it’s going to be a slow death for the property, as no new story / idea emerges to inspire people all over again.
No one complains more about SW than SW fans. So annoying, this coming from a SW lifelong fan.
Wow that sounds bad. Like every part of it
Rey is a Palpatine. Disney offed all the Skywalkers in their terrible fanfic and named SW after the now gone Skywalkers like a developer naming a street Oak Street after getting rid of all the oaks. Hopefully Star Wars’ good name can be free some day.
“Star Wars Continuing the Skywalker Saga with Spider-Man” would generate a lot more interest.
Dropping all their plans and going after a top tier filmmaker in Christopher Nolan should have been the play. Giving him total creative freedom. But they’re unwilling to learn. Maybe they need another decade of failure to get it.
I remember seeing a video of Nolan during the Oppenheimer press tour, where he had to give yes or no answers. When he got the obligatory “Would you do a Star Wars film?”, he just said “Pass.”
Given he’s not made a franchise film since he parted ways with Batman, I can’t ever see Nolan going back to franchise work. He has all the power any director would want. He’s not going to give that away to play in someone else’s sandbox.
Don’t be afraid to develop your own personality or opinions one day, champ.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI halts training of latest models as reports mount of AI agents going rogue
articles.title_zh: OpenAI halts training of latest models as reports mount of AI agents going rogue
articles.content_orig:
Decision follows disclosures that OpenAI agents searching government websites had acted in unexpected ways
OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.
The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information.
Separately, the AI evaluator Transluce said agents that appeared to come from OpenAI tried unsuccessfully to hack into a US Department of Education website, a detail that OpenAI has not confirmed.
OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training “only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards” in place, adding that it expects it will have to “hit pause” again as AI develops and other issues emerge.
Last week Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, revealed an OpenAI agent had breached the government’s national healthcare system – but said no sensitive information had been compromised.
AI labs are facing pressure from lawmakers and tech experts to slow development so they can build guardrails to stop agents from acting on their own, hacking websites and disclosing nonpublic information. The heads of both OpenAI and rival Anthropic have called for a slowdown too.
It is the second time in three months that OpenAI has halted development of its models. The first came in July after disclosure of a cyber-attack targeting AI startup Hugging Face , a now notorious incident that raised fears the industry was losing control.
In a meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping this week, Donald Trump agreed to share information on AI dangers and coordinate efforts to keep it safe. Trump believes AI fears are overblown, though, and later suggested that he plans no crackdown of his own.
The US is not going to be “putting on brakes”, Trump told reporters outside the White House. “They want to stop our progress because we’re leading China by a lot, and we’re going to keep it that way.”
The latest OpenAI incidents did not appear to involve the disclosure of any nonpublic information but were concerning enough for the company to warn the federal agencies involved.
In the education department incident, OpenAI agents found API “developer keys” to access government data, though ultimately only publicly available information was gathered.
In another case involving the securities and exchange commission, agents found information freely available to all but then posted it elsewhere on the internet, an act that went beyond what they were instructed to do.
US Securities and Exchange Commission spokesperson Kurt Hopfenspirger said on Saturday that “no nonpublic information was accessed”.
The Department of Education said earlier that it found “no evidence of any impact to our website or databases”.
Several other AI companies have disclosed incidents of their models going rogue and even hacking websites.
OpenAI’s CEO, Sam Altman, said in a social media post on Friday that the Hugging Face incident “is still the most severe event we’ve seen”.
OpenAI previously shared six other reports of “unexpected or concerning” behaviour in AI models and introduced a framework for tracking, probing and disclosing instances.

President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is seeking to cancel almost $1 billion in federal funding, sidestepping congressional approval and earning criticism from lawmakers on both sides of the aisle.
Using a controversial move known as a “pocket rescission,” Trump said he wanted to nullify $810 million in spending that Congress had approved for programs and agencies, much of which would serve immigrants, minorities, and children.
Read More: A Debt Ceiling Fight Looms in 2027. Could a Democratic Congress Make it the Last One?
Over half of the cuts would land on the Health and Human Services (HHS) Department’s Office of Refugee Resettlement, according to a request sent to House Speaker Mike Johnson on Friday. It said that rescinding the funds is “consistent with the Administration's goal of ending the use of Federal taxpayer dollars to support non-citizens, putting Americans first.”
In a statement accompanying the request, the Trump Administration also called the funds “wasteful” and “harmful.”
The Government Accountability Office (GAO), a nonpartisan government watchdog, has asserted, however, that the move is an illegal sidestepping of the constitutionally protected separation of powers—chiefly, Congress's power of the purse.
A “pocket rescission” is not a formal or legal term; it was coined to reference a “ pocket veto ,” a process in which a bill fails to become law because the President does not sign it within 10 days and Congress’s adjournment prevents its return. Similarly, the “pocket rescission” aims to withdraw allocated funding without direct congressional intervention.
The timing is important when it comes to pocket rescissions. In order to be fully effective, this “occurs when a president asks Congress to rescind (or cancel) funds very close to the end of the fiscal year—so close that the funds expire before they can be used for new obligations,” according to the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO).
The Office of Management and Budget (OMB), helmed by Director Russell Vought, submitted the requests Friday and holds that the move is valid under the 1974 Impoundment Control Act (ICA).
The Impoundment Control Act was created in response to President Richard Nixon’s heavy use of impoundments to achieve his policy goals. It has since been used to limit or regulate a president’s ability to control spending that has already been appropriated by building in 45 days of continuous congressional session. During this time, Congress is meant to review a President’s rescission requests and either approve them or see the funds released as planned.
Trump’s request to cancel $810 million in funding, however, came just five days before the end of the fiscal year on Sept. 30, all but ensuring that Congress will not have time to review the proposal in full or prevent the cuts from going into effect.
It is not the first time Trump has used this strategy to thwart spending attempts. He submitted a request on Aug. 28, 2025, to cancel $4.9 billion in foreign aid funds approved by Congress, including $3.2 billion that had been allocated to USAID . Although the move was contested, the Supreme Court last year stayed a lower court injunction requiring roughly $4 billion covered by the rescission request to be obligated.
The GAO claims that the move is illegal, writing on its website that this application of the ICA would “cede Congress’s power of the purse by allowing a president to, in effect, change the law by shortening the period of availability for fixed-period funds.”
“If Congress wanted a president to have that authority, it would need to change the law,” it continues.
Zachary Price, a professor at the University of California College of the Law, San Francisco, says that the move is an “abuse” of the ICA.
“It’s perverse to read that as, instead, creating this mechanism for unilaterally canceling funds,” Price tells TIME, adding that this interpretation is not supported by a lot of “historical practice.”
The maneuver seeks to withhold the funds until they expire at the end of the fiscal year, leaving Congress little time to respond.
In this case, Price says, it further showcases how the ICA is being manipulated.
The government “shouldn't have a lot of money left over at the end of the fiscal year if you've been spending it as you go in the way the statute contemplates,” he says.
He also points out that the American government is distinctly separated into three branches, with Congress, sitting in the legislative branch, being given the power to pass legislation—or, in this case, cancel funds that have already been appropriated. It has been explicitly separated from the authority of the executive branch and the President.
Bobby Kogan, the senior director of federal budget policy at the Center for American Progress, says it even plainer than Price: “The administration has picked a bunch of things that they hate, and they say, ‘Well, we're just not going to do those.’”
The Supreme Court’s intervention last year did not constitute a ruling on the authority of pocket rescissions, meaning that the Trump Administration's latest use of the tactic could face new legal challenges.
The largest portion of this year’s proposed cuts will target HHS programs providing nonprofit services for refugees and unaccompanied minors. Trump’s request would withdraw $567 million from those services.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was also impacted, with a request to cancel funding for nonprofits that provide mental health services and social services to migrants. Another cut targets almost $25 million that had been slated for the Department of Education’s Special Programs for Migrant Students.
The Housing and Urban Development Department’s housing counseling services are also named amid the rescissions; the Trump Administration said that the program included non-governmental organizations with “divisive and DEI-centric agendas.”
The Trump Administration also aims to cancel $15 million from a Department of Justice office that focuses on reducing racial tensions, in addition to $10 million that had been allocated to the Minority Business Development Agency, which supports minority entrepreneurs.
“I assume that they're picking money to cancel based on some political calculus about what they can get away with,” Price says. When looking at the bigger picture, he argues this is just one maneuver in several to “establish stronger executive control over spending.”
The move also risks future negotiations in Congress, Price says. He explains that this application of the ICA would make it harder for Democrats and Republicans to compromise over spending if they anticipate that the sitting President will simply swoop in and cancel funding after thoughtful agreements have been reached.
“If the executive branch can come in and effectively impose a more kind of party line view of the spending, then you know why would people agree to the package in the first place?” he asks.
The rescission has earned blowback from both Republican and Democratic lawmakers who believe that the move sidesteps Congress's authority.
Republican Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, the chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, lambasted the move on social media Friday evening , saying she would “work with my colleagues to address these illegal actions.”

articles.title_zh: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Director Champions Franchise’s First R Rating as Sequel Rocks NYFF at World Premiere: ‘Censoring’ the Action ‘Was Not an Option’
articles.content_orig:
“ Godzilla Minus Zero” blew the roof off Alice Tully Hall during its rapturous world premiere screening at the New York Film Festival . The long-awaited sequel to 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” earned rave first reactions from the press earlier in the day, and that adoration rolled right into the world premiere. The movie was met with multiple mid-screening applauses as the crowd went wild for all the kaiju mayhem on screen.
Ahead of its debut later this year, “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” has been rated R for “violent content/bloody images,” making it the first entry in the 72-year-old franchise to receive an R-rating. Director Takashi Yamazaki , returning to helm the sequel after 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” became a roaring success, says securing the rating was “essential to the film.” “Logically, as a studio — and even as a director — you want as many people from the general public to be able to see your film,” Yamazaki told Variety at the premiere Saturday afternoon. “So, an R-rating might seem like a barrier to entry, and conversations about, ‘Hey, could we have not gotten this down to PG-13?’ of course are going to happen. In spite of that, though, there were certain scenes that, for me as a director, were so essential to the film. Censoring it or cutting it was just not an option for me.”
Under MPA guidelines, viewers under 17 cannot attend an R-rated film without a parent or guardian, a restriction that has traditionally made the rating a commercial deterrent for studios releasing big-budget, four-quadrant films. That stigma has faded over the past decade, starting with the blockbuster success of 2016’s “Deadpool” ($782 million). In 2019, “Joker” ($1.07 billion) became the first R-rated film to cross the $1 billion threshold. That record was later broken by 2024’s “Deadpool & Wolverine” ($1.33 billion) — and more recently — 2026’s “The Odyssey” ($1.72 billion), which currently stands as the 17th highest-grossing film of all time worldwide.
“I think the R-rating, at one point, carried almost a negative connotation,” Yamazaki explained. “In more modern films, it actually creates a sort of expectation and excitement of, ‘Okay, well, they’re not censoring anything. The director and the cast’s voice is there, as is.’ So it is very encouraging to see other films who have preceded us that have already found a lot of success with the R-rating at the box office. Hopefully, we can continue that trend with ‘Godzilla Minus Zero.’”
Inside the world premiere screening, New York Film Festival director Dennis Lim acknowledged that the Godzilla franchise might not be the first thing people think of playing at a major film festival. And yet, “We thought it was about time to bring a giant monster movie here.”
Yamazaki took the stage to thunderous applause from the audience both before and after the screening, where he asked the crowd not to spoil any of the sequel’s many surprises on social media.
“You are the first to see this film,” the filmmaker said. “There are a lot of ‘Godzilla’ fans around the world, so let’s work together and do not do any spoilers. No spoilers, please! I am trusting all of you guys.”
Yamazaki also had the audience laughing while explaining how he never intended to create a sequel to “Godzilla Minus One.” Executives at Toho immediately started asking him about a follow-up movie once they saw the first cut of “Minus One,” a thought that made Yamazaki instantly nervous. It wasn’t until the movie opened in theaters and started to be celebrated around the world by audiences that the director realized a sequel would be a viable option.
“Toho executives are here,” the director said. “With your reactions tonight I hope they don’t offer a third movie.”

articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV met with the Bishops of France on Sunday in Lourdes, just a short distance from where Our Lady appeared to St. Bernadette Soubirous in 1858.
Thanking them for placing their ministry under the Virgin Maryâs protection, he said there is âno better way to come to Jesus than through Mary.â
Recalling Franceâs deep historical devotion to Our Lady, Pope Leo said the French people bear a living faith, which the Bishops must help grow and deepen.
He encouraged them to show courage and missionary creativity, despite todayâs challenges and human errors.
âAlways have the courage to acknowledge failings with a love of the truth and a determination to bind up wounds with the charity of the Good Shepherd,â he said.
The Church has contributed greatly to building French society, noted Pope Leo, adding that the Churchâs voice has âevery right to be heard in the public square.â
âBy its nature, it possesses a prophetic authority,â he said. âEven if it is not always understood, her voice is nonetheless needed.â
The French Church lives under a particular form of secularity ( laïcité ), which endured a turbulent history but now enjoys a more peaceful and hard-won balance, which is âgradually being called into question.â
âI urge you to remain vigilant in defending the freedom and rights of the Church to evangelize, to educate about true freedom, and to worship publicly, so that charity may be exercised visibly in the name of Jesus Christ,â he said.
Pope Leo joined the late Pope Francis in urging French Catholics to âreclaim their heritage of faith,â which finds expression in awareness of the inalienable worth of the human person and the flourishing of the arts.
As France and the world faces polarization, a decline in fraternity, and a rise in violence, the Church must remain a prophetic sign of renewal, so that society may hear the hope-filled message of the Gospel.
He encouraged the Bishops to show young people the âsure wayâ of the Gospel in doctrinal clarity and to work with them for all that is âbeautiful, true, and good.â
âTo renew hope and give fresh impetus to the Churchâs mission in France, which I earnestly desire, there is only one âroadmap,â which is always the same: to make Jesus Christ known and loved, authentically, passionately, again and again,â he said.
Pope Leo then pointed to several major challenges facing the Church in France, including Catholic education, which he said must always welcome all people while offering them an opportunity to encounter Christ.
He thanked the Bishops of France for taking âcourageous measuresâ to confront the âpainful scourge of abuse of minors committed by members of the clergy or in an ecclesial context.â
âYou must continue along the path you have begun, maintaining the greatest vigilance,â he said. âAt the same time, your clergy need to be supported and encouraged.â
Pope Leo said priests must be âeagerly wanted, welcomed, and lovedâ and that their identity as men configured to Christ should be understood by the faithful.
He noted the decline in religious vocations, especially to contemplative life, and lamented the closure of âancient and renowned monastic communities,â which have left a deep impact on France.
The Pope encouraged the Bishops to offer their full support for families of French Catholics, so that they may live their faith in Christ fully and help young people dedicate their lives to Him.
âTo give oneâs life to following Jesus along such a demanding path requires, alongside the work of grace, a special generosity, a deep-rooted faith, a sustained interior life, and a privileged closeness to him,â he said.
In conclusion, Pope Leo XIV urged the Bishops of France to remain united in charity and never descend into ideological division, which he said would render their witness in vain.
âThis unity is not a flat uniformity, but rather allows every sensibility that is authentically Catholic to converge naturally in a common profession of faith, through obedience to the legitimate Pastors and especially to the Successor of Peter,â he said. âIt is a unity that is enriched through reciprocal dialogue, rooted in faith, and expressed in the synodal style that we have been seeking to deepen in recent times.â

articles.title_orig: Russian Foreign Minister Vows Russia Will See Ukraine War Through
articles.title_zh: Russian Foreign Minister Vows Russia Will See Ukraine War Through
articles.content_orig:
The two foreign ministers met on the sidelines of the UN general assembly in New York even though relations have been frozen since the invasion. What we know on day 1,677
The foreign ministers of Russia and Germany met in New York on the sidelines of the ⁠UN general assembly , ⁠in the first such ​talks since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine . But Russia’s top diplomat dismissed Germany’s calls to ease off its “dangerous path of escalation” toward Europe, instead accusing Germany of being Ukraine’s main sponsor and seeking to be a leading military power in Europe. “Does Berlin understand what this could lead to?” the Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, asked in his speech at the gathering of world leaders on Saturday. “Didn’t they learn the lessons of world war two?”
German foreign minister, Johann ‌Wadephul, used the talks to call on Russia “to abandon the dangerous path of escalation vis-a-vis Germany, Europe, and Nato” , according to a delegation source. Wadephul said incidents such as the attempted drone attack in Leipzig would not shake Germany’s resolve to support Ukraine, according to sources.
Relations between Moscow and Berlin have been frozen since the Russian invasion , and tensions escalated further after the drone incident at Leipzig airport. In a sign of the continued frostiness, Lavrov told a press conference on Saturday “nothing new” came from the talks with his German counterpart.
“I told him that frankly … you could just have called me and said: ‘read my statement’,” Lavrov said . “He simply reiterated his official public position condemning Russia … you can judge for yourself whether that counts as dialogue or not.”
Still, the ​ministers discussed bilateral ties and the war in Ukraine, officials from ‌both sides said. Wadephul urged Lavrov to do “everything possible to reach an agreement on grain exports via the Black Sea”, a German ‌delegation source said.
In a sign of the sensitivities around meeting the Russian foreign minister , Wadephul notified his European allies of the meeting afterwards in a message seen by Reuters. “I used this opportunity to reiterate our position on Russia’s war of aggression ⁠against Ukraine and to call for an immediate and complete ceasefire, most pressingly with a focus on grain ​exports, and the energy infrastructure,” he wrote.
After the meeting Lavrov addressed world leaders at the assembly, where he defended Russia’s war in Ukraine and lobbed barbs at the west — including Germany – and criticised the militarisation of Japan. He made clear that Russia will veto any attempt by Germany and Japan for permanent seats on the UN security council. The two nations fought Russia, Britain and the US in the second world war. Writing on her personal Telegram channel, Maria Zakharova, a spokesperson for Russia’s foreign ministry, said that “tens of diplomats” had come to meet Lavrov to “shake his hand and thank Russia”.
An overwhelming majority of general assembly member nations have repeatedly condemned Russia’s invasion of Ukraine , as Wadephul noted in his own address to the assembly Saturday. “Russia’s war targets the lives of millions of innocent people, the existence of the Ukrainian state and culture and the European peace order,” he said, urging Russia to negotiating toward ending the fighting.
The talks came amid an intensifying aerial war and as Donald Trump said he hoped the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, would “settle” with Russia’s Vladimir Putin. With frontline positions largely unchanged since last year, Russia has hammered Ukraine with cruise and ballistic missiles, powerful glide bombs and jet-powered drones in recent months, while Ukraine’s long-range drones have targeted Russian oil refineries and businesses.
“It is essential that our partners not forget: Russia is escalating every single day,” Zelenskyy wrote on Saturday. “If the Russians have chosen to make their strikes even more brutal, the world must choose stronger responses to keep the war from spreading further.”
Ukrainian officials said Russian attacks killed four people on Saturday, as Russian authorities said a Ukrainian drone attack killed three.
Residents of Kyiv are preparing for power cuts, drone attacks and a bitter cold winter by stocking up on generators, food and “dry showers”, as the Ukrainian capital becomes a frontline city .
And Russia has opened a new front in its campaign against Ukraine , hitting several datacentres and internet providers in Kyiv this week in an apparent attempt to weaken the digital backbone of the economy.

articles.title_orig: Trump says he ended Biden electric vehicle rule, updated fuel economy standards
articles.title_zh: Trump says he ended Biden electric vehicle rule, updated fuel economy standards
articles.content_orig:
The Trump administration is planning to release new fuel efficiency mandates Monday that would weaken stringent rules implemented under President Biden.
President Trump pitched the changes, which he announced in December, as a way to boost the domestic auto industry and lower consumer costs. He made the original announcement standing alongside several auto executives.
“These new Standards will take the waste out of building cars in America,” Trump said in a social media post Saturday. “That means LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands on a new, beautiful, and safe car — Far better than the Environmental Monsters that we were building heretofore.”
Trump has long criticized the Biden-era rules, which were part of a set of policies to spur production and purchases of electric vehicles. EV production and sales have plummeted as a consequence of Trump administration policies, and the new changes also come as elevated fuel prices are sending ripples through the broader U.S. economy.
Trump, whose party is struggling in the polls ahead of the November midterm elections, has been under pressure to do more to address concerns about rising prices for consumer goods, particularly as oil prices have remained persistently high since the start of the Iran war.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy responded to the president’s comments Saturday with his own social media post, saying that a “major victory for America’s auto workers is COMING MONDAY.” A U.S. official confirmed that new Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards will be released Monday.
If Monday’s final rule mirrors the original proposal from last year, it would lower the fuel-economy requirement for 2031 model-year vehicles to 34.5 miles per gallon from about 50 mpg previously.
The lowered standards would represent a major win for the auto and oil industries that complained the Biden-era requirements push the bounds of available technology and effectively discourage the sale of traditional gasoline-powered vehicles in favor of electric models.
However, the changes also come as diesel prices set a record high and gasoline prices reached their highest level ever for September, extending a rally driven by the Iran war and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
Trump administration officials are studying a range of options aimed at curbing soaring fuel prices, fueled in part by political impetus as rising cost of living is undermining Republicans’ odds of retaining control of Congress after the November midterm elections. Banning diesel exports has been floated as an option, though energy experts say such a step would only offer short-term relief and eventually drive costs even higher.
“With Americans struggling to afford gasoline that is more than $4 a gallon, the Trump administration is going to force them to pay more at the pump,” said Atid Kimelman, an attorney at Natural Resources Defense Council, an environmental nonprofit group. “Oil companies will get a windfall from gutting the fuel economy standards, but the rest of us are going to be handing over more of our hard-earned paychecks to fill up the tank.”
Mijares Torres writes for Bloomberg. Bloomberg writer Ari Natter contributed to this report.

The nor’easter moving north along the mid-Atlantic and southern New England coast this weekend is bringing hazardous beach conditions, rain and gusty winds to southern Maine.
Some scattered rains began early Saturday in southern New Hampshire, coastal Maine and a few inland Maine areas. That rain will become steadier into the evening and Sunday morning and remain moderate to heavy through Monday before the storm exits the region on Tuesday, said Zack Hargrove, a meteorologist at the National Weather Service’s office in Gray.
Hargrove expects 1-2 inches of rain for most of coastal and inland Maine through Monday, but he said some areas of southwest Maine in York County could see up to 4 inches.
“That’s where the rain hotspot will definitely be,” Hargrove said.
The strongest winds will blow by the coast, where coastal flood and high surf advisories remain in effect. Hargrove said the gusts will move at 25 to 35 miles per hour, with the strongest winds Saturday night into Sunday morning. A few gusts may travel at 40 miles per hour.
“We will have water piling up with that persistent northeast flow, so we will still have to keep our eye on it for sure,” Hargrove said.
High winds and waves have already made an impact.
Jason Nappi, an independent meteorologist, said he was monitoring the storm at beaches in Kennebunk this morning, where several tourists and surfers were also out observing. At Middle Beach, he witnessed two “sneaker waves” —unusually large coastal waves that surge much higher and farther than the waves before or after it.
He said one of the waves reached several feet past the beach’s seawall and momentarily submerged a line of cars waiting in traffic on Beach Avenue, shattering the glass windows of one car and soaked the inside. He said the car had been parked in the road and abandoned by the time he approached it, and that the wave had also appeared to dent the vehicle.
Nappi said officers from the Kennebunk Police Department showed up at the scene to investigate. Kennebunk Police Chief Robert MacKenzie did not respond immediately to request for more information about the incident.
“This storm is bordering on tropical storm or subtropical storm status right now,” Nappi said. “It’s a very powerful storm, and even though it’s not close to Maine, it still has a big impact.”
Central Maine Power has been tracking the storm and will staff additional crews at some service centers, according to a CMP press release on Friday. CMP crews cannot raise bucket truck arms when winds are greater than 30 mph, but they can help clear roads blocked by downed trees.

We’ve visited the Overworld, the Nether, and the End. Now, prepare yourself for a journey to the Sift.
First announced at Gamescom and showcased in more detail at Minecraft LIVE today, The Sift is the first new dimension in Minecraft in over 14 years, and players will be able to visit it in just a few days, when Minecraft Dungeons II launches on September 29.
But on top of that, Mojang Studios confirmed that the Sift will come to Minecraft in 2027, offering an entire new dimension for you to explore, survive, and create within.
In the opening stages of Minecraft Dungeons II , players will realize something is amiss. Strange events begin to upend the natural order of the Overworld, new enemy types appear, and souls begin to fly through the world. You’ve stumbled on the Sift.
This new reality brings an entirely different, colorful new look, new mobs (both companions and threats, all unique) and, once you enter, new rules to learn. Shifting tides within the Sift can affect your character and those around you; hazardous new blocks will alter how you approach exploration; new environments will put your skills to the test.
The Sift contains new biomes – including Meadows and Carapace – but Mojang are keeping other areas a secret for players to discover when they play Minecraft Dungeons II .
All of this will get seasoned players thinking about how Minecraft itself will change once the Sift arrives. While Mojang isn’t talking too much about how to access the Sift, or how it will stand out from Dungeons II ’s expression of it, we did get a brief in-development look at the new dimension running.
Suffice it to say, if you want a sneak peek at how the Sift will work, the best way to find out more is to play Dungeons II , which will give us a taste of mobs, blocks, and biomes . And make sure to tune in for future Minecraft LIVE events to learn more about the Sift, and when it will arrive.
